children: Commodity markets traded lower on November 12, with oil prices falling more than $1 on hopes of progress in Middle East and Russia-Ukraine peace talks and gold also extended its losses after stronger-than-expected US inflation data and hawkish Fed comments reinforced expectations of a December rate hike.
Oil prices dropped more than $1 on Thursday as hopes for progress in peace talks over the Middle East and the Russia-Ukraine wars pressured the market.

Brent futures lost $1.14, or 1.2%, to $91.62 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures fell $1.04, or 1.2%, to $85.49. Brent rose about 1.4% and WTI 0.6% on Wednesday after hitting two-month lows the previous day.
Gold slipped, extending losses triggered by a high US inflation print and hawkish remarks from Federal Reserve officials that reinforced expectations of a December rate hike.
Bullion fell as much 1.2% to trade below $4,000 an ounce during US hours, as the dollar hit the highest since May 2025.
Among other precious metals, silver was up 0.5% at $51.78 an ounce, after falling earlier in the session. Platinum fell and palladium rose.

The dollar held near a one-month high against major peers in early Asian trading on Thursday, supported by growing expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike, while the yen edged toward the psychologically important 160-per-dollar level.
The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, rose 0.63% to 102.85, its highest level since October 14.

title: Commodity Corner: Oil, gold extend losses on peace hopes, hawkish Fed signals
